note.explanation: Centripetal force keeps an object moving in a circular path at constant speed. Its direction is towards the centre of the circle, while the object's velocity is along the tangent. For example, tension in a string keeps a whirled stone moving in a circle, and Earth's gravity keeps a satellite in orbit.
examples: A string provides the centripetal force for a stone being whirled in a circle.
Earth's gravitational pull provides the centripetal force for a satellite orbiting Earth.
note.checkAnswer: The force acts towards the centre; the velocity is along the tangent, so they are perpendicular.
note.simple: Centripetal force is the inward pull that keeps an object going around a circle instead of flying off in a straight line.
note.checkQuestion: In circular motion, which way does centripetal force act compared with the object's velocity?

note.answer: Centripetal force is the force that keeps an object moving in a circle at constant speed. It acts towards the centre and is perpendicular to the object's velocity.

Velocity is along the tangent and is perpendicular to centripetal force.

rationales: This is correct: friction between the clothes and drum walls provides the needed centripetal force.

rationales: At fixed mass and speed, a greater radius gives a smaller force because F_c = mv²/r.
This is correct: centripetal force is proportional to the square of speed.
The relation includes mass, so centripetal force depends on mass.
A constant speed in a circular path still requires centripetal force to change the direction of motion.

rationales: The textbook explanation says the free water molecules cannot get the required centripetal force.
This is correct: without the required inward force, the water molecules escape through the holes.
The drum continues rotating; its rotation is what helps separate water from the clothes.
The water escapes through the holes rather than gathering at the centre.

written.text: A car travels at the same speed around two curves with different radii. For which radius the car experiences more centripetal force? Prove your answer.
written.finalAnswer: The car experiences more centripetal force on the curve with the smaller radius.

explain.title: Meaning of centripetal force
explain.body: The force that causes an object to move in a circle at constant speed is called the centripetal force. It points towards the centre of the circle.

explain.title: The relation
explain.body: For mass m moving at uniform speed v in a circle of radius r, use F_c = mv²/r. Convert mass to kilograms, substitute the values and give the answer in newtons.

explain.title: Force and velocity directions
explain.body: Centripetal force acts along the radius towards the centre. Velocity acts along the tangent to the circle. A radius and a tangent at the point of contact are perpendicular.

explain.title: Sources of centripetal force
explain.body: The force can come from different sources. String tension keeps a whirled stone in a circle; Earth's gravity keeps the Moon and satellites in orbit; friction between clothes and a dryer drum helps keep the clothes moving in a circle.

mistakes: Using the mass in grams instead of converting it to kilograms.
Using r² in the denominator or forgetting to square the speed; the relation is F_c = mv²/r.
Saying that centripetal force acts along the tangent. It acts towards the centre; velocity is along the tangent.
Leaving out the unit N when giving a calculated force.
In a comparison question, saying that the larger radius gives more force. At the same mass and speed, the smaller radius gives more force.
